skill.description: Create talking-head and AI avatar videos with inference.sh models, built-in speech, lip synchronization, dubbing, and multi-presenter workflows.

skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown backticks, code fences, placeholder media URLs, or documentation links rather than executable backticks or suspicious destinations. Real risks remain in third-party package installation, remote media processing, shell command construction, remote image loading, and synthetic testimonial workflows without consent safeguards.

remediation.issue: User-provided scripts and media references are embedded in shell-quoted JSON examples.
remediation.suggestion: Write input to a temporary JSON file with a structured serializer, then pass the file without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: Testimonial and multi-presenter examples lack consent, disclosure, and likeness safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Require authorization for every likeness and voice, prohibit deceptive endorsements, and label synthetic media in published outputs.

remediation.issue: Portraits, audio, video, and scripts are processed by external inference services.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit approval before upload and warn users about provider retention, privacy, pricing, and regional compliance.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends unpinned package installation and mutable remote installation instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions and source revisions, publish integrity hashes, and avoid loading installation guidance from a moving branch.

remediation.issue: The introductory image is loaded from an external host.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle or proxy the image through the marketplace to prevent third-party requests during skill browsing.

content.user_title: Create AI Avatar and Talking Head Videos
content.value_statement: Avatar video production often requires separate speech, animation, and lip-sync tools. This skill organizes inference.sh models into reusable presenter, dubbing, and UGC workflows.
actual_capabilities: Generate talking-head videos from a portrait and written script with P-Video-Avatar.
Animate portraits from existing audio with P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, or PixVerse.
Control voice, language, delivery style, scene direction, and output resolution.
Combine portrait generation, text-to-speech, transcription, translation, and lip synchronization.
Run batch presenter variants with different voices through shell workflows.
limitations: The skill requires the belt CLI, an authenticated inference.sh account, and access to remote models.
Model availability, pricing, speed, supported voices, and output quality can change.
Media inputs must be available through URLs accepted by the selected model.
The skill does not verify likeness rights, voice consent, advertising compliance, or synthetic-media disclosure.

use_cases.title: Produce product explainers
use_cases.description: Turn an approved presenter portrait and concise script into a narrated product walkthrough.

use_cases.title: Localize training videos
use_cases.description: Transcribe a training video, translate its narration, generate speech, and synchronize the new audio.

use_cases.title: Create character dialogue
use_cases.description: Animate an authorized character image with expressive speech for game scenes or interactive prototypes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic presenter
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 720p talking-head video from [portrait URL]. Use this script: [script]. Choose a clear, neutral English voice.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first avatar video with built-in speech

prompt_templates.title: Direct voice and scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 1080p presenter video from [portrait URL] and [script]. Use an enthusiastic voice and describe a professional studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Build a dubbing workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Dub [video URL] into [language]. Transcribe, translate, generate approved speech, and synchronize it while preserving the original visual timing.

prompt_templates.title: Generate approved presenter variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three disclosed synthetic presenter variants for [campaign]. Use authorized portraits, distinct voices, consistent messaging, and vertical 1080p output.

output_examples.input: Create a neutral 720p presenter video from an authorized portrait and a 30-second onboarding script.
output: Selected P-Video-Avatar for integrated speech and portrait animation.
Prepared a neutral English voice and 720p output.
Submitted the approved portrait and onboarding script for generation.

output_examples.input: Dub an existing safety training video into Spanish using an approved replacement voice.
output: Prepared a Spanish translation for review.
Generated approved Spanish speech and synchronized it with the source video.

output_examples.input: Create three disclosed vertical presenter variants for a product campaign.
output: Prepared three authorized presenter and voice combinations.
Applied consistent campaign messaging and vertical framing.

best_practices: Use front-facing, well-lit portraits and clean audio for stable facial animation.
Confirm likeness, voice, script, and media rights before sending inputs to remote models.
Review generated speech, lip synchronization, claims, and disclosure labels before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not animate a real person without documented permission.
Do not embed unescaped user text directly inside shell-quoted input arguments.
Do not publish synthetic testimonials as genuine customer endorsements.

faq.question: Which model should I try first?
faq.answer: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar for integrated speech, style controls, and 720p or 1080p output.

faq.question: Can I use recorded audio instead of text?
faq.answer: Yes. P-Video-Avatar and the listed lip-sync models accept audio URLs with compatible portrait inputs.

faq.question: Can this skill dub an existing video?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow combines transcription, translation, speech generation, and LatentSync.

faq.question: Does the skill work without inference.sh?
faq.answer: No. It relies on the belt CLI, an authenticated account, and remotely hosted inference applications.

faq.question: Does it guarantee model pricing or speed?
faq.answer: No. The document includes estimates, but providers can change prices, performance, availability, and limits.

faq.question: What permissions are required for avatar media?
faq.answer: Obtain explicit rights for every likeness, voice, script, and source video. Add clear synthetic-media disclosures where required.
